why: Stage 24 established that supported vocabulary expansion is exhausted and that the series-overlap target is a corpus question, not a generator one. The generator is frozen while the corpus is investigated, and this file is what 'frozen' means: the numbers below are re-derived by scripts/validate-est-baseline.mjs on every CI run, so drift is a failure rather than a discovery.

capacity.ceilingNote: The bound is a function of the realised (family, band) demand profile, which shifts slightly with the scheduling policy. 0.463 is the profile under the plain seriesLedger, 0.479 under policy D — the run the readiness gate grades. Quoting one without the other is how a range becomes a false precision.

frozen.note: ESTM1-2026-A lives outside this repository. The md5 is recorded so a session can check it has not been touched; the payload itself is never committed.

corpus.why: Stage 26 checked whether additional official EST reference forms had arrived. They had not. The inventory is recorded as hashes and publisher test numbers — never content — so a later session can tell at a glance whether the corpus has actually grown rather than re-deriving it from filenames.
corpus.source: EST I Practice Guide — Math, 2026 Specifications (publisher's own practice book, five sample tests)

knownObtainableNotHeld.note: The guide contains five sample tests and its own cover says so. Test 4 is the one form we do not hold, and it is official, same publisher, same 2026 specification. It is the only certain +1.

excluded.what: 3 College Board digital SAT practice tests (4, 8, 10)
excluded.reason: official, but a different exam: module-structured, 27 questions per module, student-produced responses. EST I Math is 50 MCQ in one 75-minute section. Merging them would break the longitudinal comparability the coding standard exists to protect.
not an official published form. Excluded permanently by standing instruction and by this phase's own corpus rules.
